source.title: Observational Overfitting in Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Xing-You Song; Yiding Jiang; Stephen Tu; Yilun Du; Behnam Neyshabur

record.tranche_reason: Tests how architecture, width/depth, and explicit regularization affect train–test generalization gaps in RL using constructed observation-space tasks, rather than the supervised-learning setups named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Own results include LQR, projected Gym, deconvolutional memorization, CoinRun architecture and overparameterization, explicit regularization, and margin-measure analyses. Cited supervised-learning findings are not treated as rows. Values in figures without textual values are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The study measures reinforcement-learning reward generalization under observation changes. None of its results tests the specified versions: it does not compare random versus natural labels, establish widening beyond zero training error, compare convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, compare optimizers or batch sizes, manipulate dropout, measure magnitude-aware sharpness, or remove examples selected by memorization influence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors isolate observational overfitting, report that architectural overparameterization can improve generalization in LQR, projected Gym, and CoinRun, and conclude that the tested supervised-learning-inspired norm bounds do not explain those RL effects. They leave extension to off-policy and evolutionary methods unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Reinforcement-learning policies trained with exact gradient descent for LQR or PPO for projected Gym and CoinRun; synthetic observation projections and RL reward generalization replace supervised classification on natural labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Environment dynamics, architecture depth and width, activation (ReLU versus Tanh), residual layers, observation noise dimension, and whether observations expose only gθ(s).

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the Sonic scoreboard increased test reward from 1052 to 1141 for NatureCNN and from 1130 to 1250 for IMPALA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing a spurious visual feature can improve RL transfer to unseen levels.

fits_no_version.finding: Wider or deeper linear LQR policies had smaller generalization gaps and smaller end-to-end norms without increased expressiveness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural overparameterization can improve reward generalization in projected LQR.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher nuisance-observation dimension increased the nonconvex LQR generalization gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher-dimensional nuisance observations can worsen observational overfitting in LQR.

fits_no_version.finding: Projected Gym architecture benefits depended on task and activation; deeper Tanh policies could suffer poor training, while residual layers helped.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL generalization gains from architectural changes depend on activation, environment, and optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: Gym-Deconv reproduced the NatureCNN, IMPALA, IMPALA-LARGE generalization ranking, and CoinRun rewards varied across architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture influences RL reward generalization on synthetic observations and CoinRun.

fits_no_version.finding: Policies differed in their capacity to memorize nuisance-only observations; the larger IMPALA-LARGE could memorize less than smaller architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture can constrain memorization in constructed RL tasks despite increased parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Overparameterized MLPs improved CoinRun reward generalization with unlimited training levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP overparameterization can improve RL performance when training levels are continually generated.

fits_no_version.finding: Raw norms and tested norm-based bounds poorly explained RL generalization; state-action margins had conceptual limitations as reward predictors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised-learning norm and margin measures need qualification when applied to RL reward generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: The one-step LQR theorem decomposed expected population error into minimum-norm-solution and random-initialization contributions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite observation samples and initialization can produce a persistent generalization gap in projected one-step LQR.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicit norm penalties reduced the synthetic LQR generalization gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Norm regularization can reduce observational overfitting in projected LQR.

record.problems: Several principal architecture and width/depth results are available only as plots without numerical values in the supplied text. Many results are specific to synthetic observation projections or RL reward metrics and do not directly test the supervised-learning claim. The CoinRun experiment has changing level dynamics and is not the fixed-dynamics setting used in the projected environments.
record.rows_left_out: None. The table's 16 CoinRun-100 architecture rows are kept separately; within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Entire version: no fixed random-label versus natural-label classification experiment or chance-level held-out comparison.
Entire specified version: no demonstrated zero-training-error width threshold followed by further widening and classification test-error measurement.
Entire version: no matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected image-classification comparison, local-connectivity isolation, or convolutional initialization transfer.
Entire version: no adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
Entire version: no batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or compensating training recipes.
Entire version: no dropout intervention and held-out classification comparison.
Entire version: no magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measurement or comparison of its ranking with norm and margin measures.
Entire version: no removal of examples selected by memorization influence and retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not judgments that the reported RL effects are unreadable or absent. The study supplies related evidence but no version-specific verdicts. The record's ICLR 2019 publication attribution is not established by the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels in supervised classification or natural-label test accuracy versus chance.
Tests overparameterization and generalization in RL, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; no reported double-descent interpolation-threshold test.

Compares convolutional architectures in synthetic Gym-Deconv settings, but does not compare convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers trained from scratch on the listed image datasets or isolate local connectivity.
Tests state-action margin and norm-based measures against RL generalization, not magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: MLP policy
rows.operation_detail: Compared state-action margin distributions and raw network norms as training progressed.
rows.value: Raw norms are a poor way to predict generalization; they generally increase as training begins to plateau.
rows.note: This bears on the broader generalization-measure question, but not magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: Poor predictive performance of raw policy norms does not test magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: MLP policy
rows.operation_detail: Measured state-action margin distributions over on-policy replay-buffer samples.
rows.value: The distribution converges to a fixed distribution long after training has plateaued; authors say it is not fully correlated with RL generalization on total reward.
rows.note: Tests margin distributions as candidate predictors; not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure specified by V7.
rows.check: State-action margin distributions are not magnitude-aware sharpness. The incomplete-correlation statement is a conceptual qualification, not a reported numerical correlation.

rows.subject: LQR policy K
rows.operation_detail: Compared bounds based on policy norms and related measures with the generalization gap across depth and width.
rows.value: Current norm-based bounds have very little predictive power; current norm measures are too loose for the RL case.
rows.note: Not a magnitude-aware sharpness comparison.
rows.check: Loose norm-based RL bounds do not challenge V7's correlation involving magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: LQR policy K
rows.size_stated: n = 10, p = 1000 default figure settings; general formula stated
rows.operation_detail: Ran gradient descent on m training observation projections from random Gaussian initialization in the one-step LQR case.
rows.value: Theorem 1 gives an expression depending on n, m, p, and ψ²; numerical values not stated
rows.uncertainty: Expectation over randomness of samples and initialization
rows.note: Explicit analysis demonstrates a generalization gap in this RL toy setting; not one of the listed supervised-learning versions.
rows.check: The theorem concerns projected one-step LQR, outside all versions. Its training projections are mutually orthogonal blocks from one Haar-random orthogonal matrix, not independent projection draws.

rows.subject: LQR policy K
rows.operation_detail: Applied explicit norm-based penalties to layer norms.
rows.note: Text states explicit regularization reduces the gap, while noting this may exploit the synthetic-task bias.
rows.check: Norm penalties in LQR do not test dropout or any other listed intervention.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LQR and CoinRun MLP overparameterization experiments
reader_labels.reason: Added linear layers, increased width, and overparameterized CoinRun MLPs reduce the generalization gap or improve generalization (R3, R5, R36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Benefits depend on environment, activation, and whether width or depth is changed; one reported Tanh depth setting also incurs subpar training performance (R7–R10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NatureCNN, IMPALA and IMPALA-LARGE on Gym-Deconv
reader_labels.reason: The reported convolutional architecture ranking is consistent across Gym-Deconv and CoinRun, with IMPALA-LARGE best on Gym-Deconv (R11–R13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The table reports varying train/test rewards and the paper identifies IMPALA-LARGE-BN as the highest-test-reward default network, but no fully connected comparison or classification error measure is tested (R20–R35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: RL margin and norm measures in CoinRun and LQR
reader_labels.reason: Raw norms predict poorly and margin distributions are not fully correlated with total-reward generalization; the paper's tested measures are not magnitude-aware sharpness (R37–R39).
